source.text: חַכְמ֣וֹת נָ֭שִׁים בָּנְתָ֣ה בֵיתָ֑הּ וְ֝אִוֶּ֗לֶת בְּיָדֶ֥יהָ תֶהֶרְסֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] wise of women builds her house, but folly with her hands tears it down.

en.L: [The] wise among women builds her house, but folly tears it down with her own hands.
en.B: A wise woman builds up her home, but a foolish one pulls it down with her own hands.
en.R: A wise woman makes her home strong. A foolish woman destroys her own home.

decisions.choice: wise women ... folly: a wise woman and a foolish one
decisions.reason: The text reads "the wise of women" and then "folly" as subject. It may recall Wisdom who built her house (9:1) and Folly (9:13), seen in ordinary women's lives.

source.text: הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּ֭יָשְׁרוֹ יְרֵ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וּנְל֖וֹז דְּרָכָ֣יו בּוֹזֵֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [One] walking in his uprightness fears YHWH, but [one] crooked [in] his ways despises him.

en.L: Whoever walks in {{gender:their|his}} uprightness fears {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but whoever is devious in {{gender:their|his}} ways despises {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Whoever lives uprightly fears {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but whoever goes crooked ways despises {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: People who live honestly show that they honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. People who are dishonest show that they hate {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: fears ... despises: how one lives shows how one regards God
decisions.reason: A person's way of life is a statement about God (14:31; 17:5).

source.text: בְּֽפִי־אֱ֭וִיל חֹ֣טֶר גַּאֲוָ֑ה וְשִׂפְתֵ֥י חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים תִּשְׁמוּרֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: In [the] mouth of a fool [is] a rod of pride, but [the] lips of wise [people] will preserve them.

en.L: In [the] mouth of a fool [is] a rod of pride, but [the] lips of [the] wise will preserve them.
en.B: A fool's talk is a rod for his own back, the fruit of his pride, but the words of the wise keep them safe.
en.R: Proud fools get themselves into trouble by what they say. The words of wise people keep them safe.

decisions.choice: a rod of pride: a shoot of pride, or a rod for pride
decisions.reason: The word (hoter) is a shoot or branch (Isaiah 11:1), or a rod. The fool's proud words either grow from pride or bring a beating on him.

source.text: בְּאֵ֣ין אֲ֭לָפִים אֵב֣וּס בָּ֑ר וְרָב־תְּ֝בוּא֗וֹת בְּכֹ֣חַ שֽׁוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: When there are no oxen, [the] manger [is] clean, but much produce [is] by [the] strength of an ox.

en.L: Where [there are] no oxen, [the] manger [is] clean, but much harvest [comes] by [the] strength of an ox.
en.B: Without oxen the feeding trough stays clean, but it takes a strong ox to bring a big harvest.
en.R: If you do not own oxen, you do not have to clean up after them. But you need strong oxen to grow a big crop.

decisions.choice: oxen ... harvest: work animals bring mess and gain
decisions.reason: Oxen pulled the plow. They cost food and cleaning, but without them there is little harvest.

source.text: עֵ֣ד אֱ֭מוּנִים לֹ֣א יְכַזֵּ֑ב וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים עֵ֣ד שָֽׁקֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness breathes out lies.

en.L: A faithful witness does not lie, but a false witness breathes out lies.
en.B: An honest witness does not deceive, but a false witness pours out lies.
en.R: An honest witness does not lie in court. A dishonest witness tells one lie after another.

decisions.choice: witness: in court, as in 12:17

source.text: בִּקֶּשׁ־לֵ֣ץ חָכְמָ֣ה וָאָ֑יִן וְדַ֖עַת לְנָב֣וֹן נָקָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: A mocker seeks wisdom, and there is none, but knowledge to [one] understanding [is] easy.

en.L: A mocker seeks wisdom and [finds] none, but knowledge [comes] easily to [one who] understands.
en.B: A mocker goes looking for wisdom and comes up empty, but a person of understanding learns with ease.
en.R: People who make fun of others cannot find wisdom, even if they look for it. But learning is easy for people who understand.

decisions.choice: a mocker seeks wisdom: but not humbly
decisions.reason: The mocker wants wisdom without being corrected (9:7–8), so it eludes him.

source.text: לֵ֣ךְ מִ֭נֶּגֶד לְאִ֣ישׁ כְּסִ֑יל וּבַל־יָ֝דַ֗עְתָּ שִׂפְתֵי־דָֽעַת׃

records.literal_gloss: Go from before a foolish person, and you will not have known lips of knowledge.

en.L: Go from [the] presence of a foolish person, for you will not find lips of knowledge [there].
en.B: Stay away from a fool, for you will not hear knowledge from his lips.
en.R: Stay away from foolish people. You will not learn anything from them.

decisions.choice: you will not have known: there is nothing to learn there
decisions.reason: The second line may say why to leave (you will find no knowledge) or what happens if you stay.

source.text: חָכְמַ֣ת עָ֭רוּם הָבִ֣ין דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וְאִוֶּ֖לֶת כְּסִילִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] wisdom of a prudent [person] [is] to understand his way, but [the] folly of fools [is] deceit.

en.L: [The] wisdom of [the] prudent [is] to understand {{gender:their|his}} way, but [the] folly of fools [is] deceit.
en.B: The prudent are wise because they think about where they are going, but the folly of fools is self-deception.
en.R: Wise people think carefully about how they live. Foolish people fool themselves.

decisions.choice: deceit: deceiving themselves, or others
decisions.reason: The fool's folly misleads, most of all the fool himself (verse 12).

source.text: אֱ֭וִלִים יָלִ֣יץ אָשָׁ֑ם וּבֵ֖ין יְשָׁרִ֣ים רָצֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Fools mock guilt, but among [the] upright [is] favor.

en.L: Fools mock at guilt, but among [the] upright [there is] favor.
en.B: Fools make light of guilt, but among the upright there is goodwill.
en.R: Fools laugh when they do wrong and do not try to make it right. Good people want to make peace.

decisions.choice: guilt: guilt, or the offering to make amends
decisions.reason: The word (asham) is guilt and also the offering to set it right (Leviticus 5:15). Fools scoff at making amends; the upright seek goodwill.

decisions.choice: fools mock: a singular verb with a plural subject
decisions.reason: The verb is singular, perhaps "each fool mocks".

source.text: לֵ֗ב י֭וֹדֵעַ מָרַּ֣ת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וּ֝בְשִׂמְחָת֗וֹ לֹא־יִתְעָ֥רַב זָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: A heart knows [the] bitterness of its soul, and in its joy a stranger does not share.

en.L: [The] heart knows its own bitterness, and in its joy a stranger does not share.
en.B: Each heart knows its own sorrow, and no outsider can share its joy.
en.R: Only you know how sad you really are. No one else can fully share your happiness either.

decisions.choice: each heart alone: the privacy of feeling
decisions.reason: A saying about how much each person carries alone, in sorrow and in joy.

source.text: בֵּ֣ית רְ֭שָׁעִים יִשָּׁמֵ֑ד וְאֹ֖הֶל יְשָׁרִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] house of wicked [people] will be destroyed, but [the] tent of upright [people] will flourish.

en.L: [The] house of [the] wicked will be destroyed, but [the] tent of [the] upright will flourish.
en.B: The house of the wicked will be wiped out, but the tent of the upright will thrive.
en.R: The homes of evil people will be destroyed. The homes of good people will do well.

decisions.choice: house ... tent: a solid house against a tent
decisions.reason: The irony: the wicked's house falls, while the upright's tent stands (12:7).

source.text: יֵ֤שׁ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יָ֭שָׁר לִפְנֵי־אִ֑ישׁ וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ דַּרְכֵי־מָֽוֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: There is a way right before a person, but its end [is the] ways of death.

en.L: There is a way [that seems] right to a person, but its end [is the] way to death.
en.B: There is a road that looks right to a person, but at the end of it is death.
en.R: Some ways of living seem right to people, but they lead to death.

decisions.choice: repeated in 16:25
decisions.reason: The same saying returns in 16:25. Compare 12:15 and 3:7.

source.text: גַּם־בִּשְׂח֥וֹק יִכְאַב־לֵ֑ב וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּשִׂמְחָ֣ה תוּגָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Even in laughter a heart is in pain, and its end, joy, [is] grief.

en.L: Even in laughter [the] heart may ache, and [the] end of joy [may be] grief.
en.B: Even while laughing the heart may ache, and joy can end in sorrow.
en.R: Sometimes people laugh even when they are sad. And happiness can turn to sadness.

decisions.choice: laughter ... grief: feelings mixed and passing
decisions.reason: Compare verse 10 and Ecclesiastes 7:3–4.

source.text: מִדְּרָכָ֣יו יִ֭שְׂבַּע ס֣וּג לֵ֑ב וּ֝מֵעָלָ֗יו אִ֣ישׁ טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: From his ways will be satisfied [the] backslider of heart, and from himself a good person.

en.L: [The] backslider in heart will be filled with {{gender:their|his}} own ways, and a good person [with what is] {{gender:their|his}} own.
en.B: The faithless will get their fill of their own ways, and the good will be rewarded for theirs.
en.R: People who turn away from God will get what they deserve. Good people will be rewarded for the good they do.

decisions.choice: backslider in heart: one who has turned away
decisions.reason: The word (sug) means to turn back or away (Psalm 80:19).

decisions.choice: from himself: from his own deeds
alternatives: from above him (with a small change)
decisions.reason: "From upon himself" is unusual; it most likely means from his own conduct.

source.text: פֶּ֭תִי יַאֲמִ֣ין לְכָל־דָּבָ֑ר וְ֝עָר֗וּם יָבִ֥ין לַאֲשֻׁרֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: A simple [person] believes every word, but a prudent [person] considers his step.

en.L: [The] simple believes every word, but [the] prudent considers {{gender:their|his}} steps.
en.B: The naive believe everything they hear, but the prudent watch where they are going.
en.R: Foolish people believe everything they hear. Wise people think carefully before they act.

decisions.choice: the simple believes everything: the definition of 1:4
decisions.reason: This is what makes the simple simple.

source.text: חָכָ֣ם יָ֭רֵא וְסָ֣ר מֵרָ֑ע וּ֝כְסִ֗יל מִתְעַבֵּ֥ר וּבוֹטֵֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: A wise [person] fears and turns from evil, but a fool is arrogant and confident.

en.L: [The] wise is cautious and turns from evil, but a fool is reckless and sure of himself.
en.B: The wise are careful and turn away from evil, but a fool is reckless and overconfident.
en.R: Wise people are careful and stay away from evil. Fools rush ahead without thinking.

decisions.choice: fears: is cautious, or fears the LORD
decisions.reason: "Fears" here may mean caution, or the fear of the LORD (3:7).

decisions.choice: reckless: overbearing, carried away
decisions.reason: The verb (hitabber) means to be overbearing or to fly into a rage (20:2; 26:17).

source.text: קְֽצַר־אַ֭פַּיִם יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אִוֶּ֑לֶת וְאִ֥ישׁ מְ֝זִמּ֗וֹת יִשָּׂנֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: [One] short of anger does folly, and a person of schemes is hated.

en.L: [One] quick-tempered does folly, and a person of schemes is hated.
en.B: Someone with a short temper acts foolishly, and the one who schemes is hated.
en.R: People who get angry quickly do foolish things. People who plan evil are hated.

decisions.choice: short of anger: quick-tempered
decisions.reason: "Short of nostrils" is quick to anger; "long of nostrils" (verse 29) is patient.

source.text: נָחֲל֣וּ פְתָאיִ֣ם אִוֶּ֑לֶת וַֽ֝עֲרוּמִ֗ים יַכְתִּ֥רוּ דָֽעַת׃

records.literal_gloss: Simple [people] inherit folly, but prudent [people] are crowned [with] knowledge.

en.L: [The] simple inherit folly, but [the] prudent are crowned [with] knowledge.
en.B: The naive end up with folly as their inheritance, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
en.R: Foolish people end up even more foolish. Wise people end up with more knowledge.

decisions.choice: crowned: surrounded, or crowned
decisions.reason: The verb (katar) means to surround, and in this form to crown (Psalm 142:8).

source.text: שַׁח֣וּ רָ֭עִים לִפְנֵ֣י טוֹבִ֑ים וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים עַֽל־שַׁעֲרֵ֥י צַדִּֽיק׃

records.literal_gloss: Evil [people] bow before good [people], and wicked [people] at [the] gates of [the] righteous.

en.L: [The] evil bow before [the] good, and [the] wicked at [the] gates of [the] righteous.
en.B: In the end the evil bow low to the good, and the wicked come begging at the doors of the righteous.
en.R: In the end, evil people will bow down to good people.

decisions.choice: bow at the gates: come begging
decisions.reason: The picture is of the wicked coming to the doors of the righteous for help (1 Samuel 2:36).

source.text: גַּם־לְ֭רֵעֵהוּ יִשָּׂ֣נֵא רָ֑שׁ וְאֹהֲבֵ֖י עָשִׁ֣יר רַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Even by his neighbor [the] poor is hated, but those loving [the] rich [are] many.

en.L: [The] poor is disliked even by {{gender:their|his}} neighbor, but [the] rich [have] many friends.
en.B: The poor are shunned even by their neighbors, but the rich have plenty of friends.
en.R: Poor people are not liked even by their neighbors. But rich people have many friends.

decisions.choice: an observation, not approval
decisions.reason: The saying states how people behave (19:4, 7). Verse 21 gives God's view.

source.text: בָּז־לְרֵעֵ֥הוּ חוֹטֵ֑א וּמְחוֹנֵ֖ן עֲנָוִ֣ים אַשְׁרָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: [One] despising his neighbor sins, but [one] showing favor [to the] humble, how blessed [is] he.

en.L: Whoever despises {{gender:their|his}} neighbor sins, but whoever is kind to [the] humble, how blessed [is] {{gender:that one|he}}.
en.B: To look down on a neighbor is a sin, but how blessed is the one who is kind to the humble.
en.R: It is wrong to look down on your neighbor. God blesses people who are kind to humble people.

decisions.choice: the humble, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: As in 3:34, the written consonants (ketiv) read "the poor" and the scribes' reading (qere) "the humble"; the two are often the same people in Scripture.

decisions.choice: how blessed: as in 3:13
decisions.reason: Verse 21 answers verse 20: God sees the poor differently.

source.text: הֲֽלוֹא־יִ֭תְעוּ חֹ֣רְשֵׁי רָ֑ע וְחֶ֥סֶד וֶ֝אֱמֶ֗ת חֹ֣רְשֵׁי טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not [those] devising evil go astray? But loyalty and faithfulness [belong to those] devising good.

en.L: Do not those who plot evil go astray? But loyal love and faithfulness [belong to] those who plan good.
en.B: Surely those who plot evil go astray, but those who plan good find loyal love and faithfulness.
en.R: People who plan to do evil lose their way. People who plan to do good are loved and trusted.

decisions.choice: loyal love and faithfulness: as in 3:3
decisions.reason: They may be shown to those who plan good, by God and others, or be their own character.

source.text: בְּכָל־עֶ֭צֶב יִהְיֶ֣ה מוֹתָ֑ר וּדְבַר־שְׂ֝פָתַ֗יִם אַךְ־לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: In all toil there is profit, but [the] word of lips [leads] only to lack.

en.L: In all toil there is profit, but mere talk [leads] only to poverty.
en.B: All hard work brings a profit, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
en.R: If you work hard, you will gain something. If you only talk, you will end up poor.

decisions.choice: a word of lips: empty talk
decisions.reason: Talk with no work behind it (2 Kings 18:20).

source.text: עֲטֶ֣רֶת חֲכָמִ֣ים עָשְׁרָ֑ם אִוֶּ֖לֶת כְּסִילִ֣ים אִוֶּֽלֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] crown of wise [people] [is] their wealth; [the] folly of fools [is] folly.

en.L: [The] crown of [the] wise [is] their wealth; [the] folly of fools [is] folly.
en.B: Wealth is a crown for the wise, but the folly of fools brings only folly.
en.R: Wise people are honored for what they have. Fools only become more foolish.

decisions.choice: folly is folly: fools gain nothing but more folly
alternatives: the garland of fools is folly (with a small change)
decisions.reason: The repetition is striking. Many read "the garland of fools is folly" to match the crown of the first line.

source.text: מַצִּ֣יל נְ֭פָשׁוֹת עֵ֣ד אֱמֶ֑ת וְיָפִ֖חַ כְּזָבִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: A true witness delivers lives, but [one who] breathes out lies [is] deceit.

en.L: A true witness saves lives, but one who breathes out lies [is a] deceiver.
en.B: A truthful witness saves lives, but one who pours out lies is a traitor.
en.R: An honest witness can save someone's life. A witness who lies betrays people.

decisions.choice: saves lives: in a court case
decisions.reason: A life could depend on testimony (Deuteronomy 19:15–19).

source.text: בְּיִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מִבְטַח־עֹ֑ז וּ֝לְבָנָ֗יו יִהְיֶ֥ה מַחְסֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: In [the] fear of YHWH [is] confidence of strength, and to his children there will be a refuge.

en.L: In [the] fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] strong confidence, and for {{gender:their|his}} children there will be a refuge.
en.B: Whoever fears {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has a secure fortress, and their children will have a refuge.
en.R: People who honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe feel safe. Their children will be safe too.

decisions.choice: his children: the children of the one who fears the LORD
decisions.reason: "His" most likely refers to the person who fears the LORD; it could refer to the LORD, whose children find refuge in him.

source.text: יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים לָ֝ס֗וּר מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי מָֽוֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] fear of YHWH [is] a fountain of life, to turn aside from snares of death.

en.L: [The] fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] a fountain of life, to turn [one] aside from [the] snares of death.
en.B: The fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is a spring of life, steering people away from the traps of death.
en.R: Honoring {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe gives life. It keeps people away from things that lead to death.

decisions.choice: as 13:14, with the fear of the LORD
decisions.reason: 13:14 says the same of the teaching of the wise.

source.text: בְּרָב־עָ֥ם הַדְרַת־מֶ֑לֶךְ וּבְאֶ֥פֶס לְ֝אֹ֗ם מְחִתַּ֥ת רָזֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: In a multitude of people [is the] glory of a king, but in lack of people [is the] ruin of a ruler.

en.L: In [the] multitude of people [is the] glory of a king, but without people a ruler [is] ruined.
en.B: A king's glory is in having many people; without people a ruler is ruined.
en.R: A king is great when he rules many people. A ruler with no people has nothing.

decisions.choice: a king's glory: a large, thriving population
decisions.reason: A king's strength lay in his people; their well-being is his honor.

source.text: אֶ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם רַב־תְּבוּנָ֑ה וּקְצַר־ר֝֗וּחַ מֵרִ֥ים אִוֶּֽלֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: [One] long of anger [has] great understanding, but [one] short of spirit exalts folly.

en.L: [One] slow to anger [has] great understanding, but [one] quick-tempered exalts folly.
en.B: Patience shows great understanding, but a quick temper puts folly on display.
en.R: People who are slow to get angry are very wise. People who get angry quickly show how foolish they are.

decisions.choice: long of anger: patient
decisions.reason: See verse 17.

source.text: חַיֵּ֣י בְ֭שָׂרִים לֵ֣ב מַרְפֵּ֑א וּרְקַ֖ב עֲצָמ֣וֹת קִנְאָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] life of [the] body [is] a heart of health, but rottenness of bones [is] envy.

en.L: A heart at peace [is the] life of [the] body, but envy [is] rot in [the] bones.
en.B: A calm heart gives life to the body, but envy is decay in the bones.
en.R: Being calm and at peace keeps your body healthy. But jealousy is like a disease that eats away your bones.

decisions.choice: envy: jealousy, passion
decisions.reason: The word (qinah) is jealousy or burning passion (6:34).

source.text: עֹ֣שֵֽׁקדָּ֭ל חֵרֵ֣ף עֹשֵׂ֑הוּ וּ֝מְכַבְּד֗וֹ חֹנֵ֥ן אֶבְיֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: [One] oppressing [the] poor insults his Maker, but [one] showing favor [to the] needy honors him.

en.L: Whoever oppresses [the] poor insults {{gender:their|his}} Maker, but whoever is kind to [the] needy honors {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Whoever oppresses the poor insults the One who made them, but kindness to the needy honors {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: If you are cruel to poor people, you insult God, who made them. If you are kind to people in need, you honor God.

decisions.choice: his Maker: God, who made rich and poor
decisions.reason: God made the poor as he made everyone (22:2; Job 31:15). To oppress them is to insult him; to help them honors him (19:17; Matthew 25:40).

decisions.choice: his Maker: the oppressor's Maker or the poor man's
decisions.reason: "His" may point to the oppressor or to the poor. Either way, God is the Maker of both.

source.text: בְּֽ֭רָעָתוֹ יִדָּחֶ֣ה רָשָׁ֑ע וְחֹסֶ֖ה בְמוֹת֣וֹ צַדִּֽיק׃

records.literal_gloss: By his wickedness a wicked [person] is thrust down, but [the] righteous [person] takes refuge in his death.

en.L: [The] wicked is thrust down by {{gender:their|his}} wickedness, but [the] righteous takes refuge in {{gender:their|his}} death.
en.B: The wicked are brought down by their own evil, but the righteous have a refuge even in death.
en.R: Evil people are destroyed by their own evil. But good people trust God even when they die.

decisions.choice: in his death, as the Hebrew text has it
alternatives: in his integrity (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "in his integrity", which differs by two letters in Hebrew. As it stands, the Hebrew expresses hope beyond death.

decisions.choice: trust God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the refuge, which the Hebrew implies (14:26).

source.text: בְּלֵ֣ב נָ֭בוֹן תָּנ֣וּחַ חָכְמָ֑ה וּבְקֶ֥רֶב כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים תִּוָּדֵֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: In [the] heart of [one] understanding wisdom rests, and in [the] inner part of fools it is made known.

en.L: Wisdom rests in [the] heart of [one who] understands, and in [the] midst of fools it is made known.
en.B: Wisdom is at home in the heart of the discerning, and even among fools it makes itself known.
en.R: Wisdom lives in the hearts of people who understand. Even fools can see it.

decisions.choice: it is made known: wisdom shows itself even among fools
alternatives: it is not known (the ancient Greek)
decisions.reason: The line is unclear. It may mean that wisdom is recognized even among fools, or (with the ancient Greek) that fools do not know it.

source.text: צְדָקָ֥ה תְרֽוֹמֵֽם־גּ֑וֹי וְחֶ֖סֶד לְאֻמִּ֣ים חַטָּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin [is] a disgrace to peoples.

en.L: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin [is] a disgrace to any people.
en.B: Righteousness lifts a nation up, but sin brings disgrace on any people.
en.R: A nation becomes great when its people do what is right. Sin brings shame on any nation.

decisions.choice: disgrace: a different word from hesed, "loyal love"
decisions.reason: The word spelled hesed here is a rare word meaning shame or reproach (Leviticus 20:17), not the common word for loyal love.

source.text: רְֽצוֹן־מֶ֭לֶךְ לְעֶ֣בֶד מַשְׂכִּ֑יל וְ֝עֶבְרָת֗וֹ תִּהְיֶ֥ה מֵבִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] favor of a king [is] for a servant acting wisely, but his fury [is for one] acting shamefully.

en.L: A king's favor [goes] to a servant who acts wisely, but his wrath [falls on one] who acts shamefully.
en.B: A king shows favor to a wise servant, but his anger falls on one who disgraces him.
en.R: A king is pleased with a servant who acts wisely. But he is angry with one who brings him shame.

decisions.choice: a king's servant: a royal official
decisions.reason: Many sayings in chapters 14–16 are about life at a king's court.
